plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no execution)

Title: Does MinED alignment outperform EM alignment on BBH?

RQ: When used as the candidate-selection (alignment) criterion over N sampled outputs per question, does MinED (Minimum Edit Distance) selection yield higher exact-match accuracy on BBH than EM (Exact Matching) selection?

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1. DECLARED FIXED ELEMENTS (from task context)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- Two arms compared: EM (Exact Matching) alignment criterion vs. MinED (Minimum Edit Distance) alignment criterion.
- Evaluation benchmark: BBH, full benchmark — 23 multiple-choice (MC) tasks + 4 free-form generation tasks (27 total), spanning the BBH task categories (setup_15 category list to be applied as printed in the source table).
- Deliverable is a design only; no experiment is run and no results are claimed.
- Final scoring metric: exact-match-to-gold accuracy, identical in both arms.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. DECLARED DESIGN ASSUMPTIONS (assumptions are stated, not verified — no source topics resolve them)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- A1 (declared, load-bearing): EM serves as the alignment/selection criterion being compared against MinED — i.e., EM arm selects among the sampled candidates using exact-matching-based consensus (majority/mode selection: pick the candidate string that exactly matches the largest number of other candidates) — while exact-match-to-gold is the common final accuracy metric in BOTH arms. Without A1 the question is ill-posed (if EM were only the metric, MinED could not "outperform" it as a criterion).
- A2: MinED selects the candidate minimizing an edit-distance objective over the candidate pool; the exact formulation is uncertain, so the design includes a sensitivity analysis over MinED variants (Section 6) rather than treating this as a blocker.
- A3: On MC tasks, candidates are short (answer letters), so MinED ≈ mode selection; the discriminating power of the experiment concentrates on the 4 free-form tasks. The design therefore pre-registers the free-form subset as a secondary endpoint (Section 7).
- A4: One open-source/instruction-tuned model family is used for all arms (exact model is a free design choice; the comparison is within-model, so results do not hinge on model identity). Sampling uses temperature T > 0 (e.g., T = 0.7) to produce a non-degenerate candidate pool.
- A5: Chain-of-thought prompting per standard BBH protocol (3-shot CoT prompts from the official BBH repo), identical across arms.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3.1 Structure: within-question paired comparison.
For every question q in all 27 BBH tasks:
  Step 1 — Sample N candidates: y_1..y_N ~ model(·|prompt_q), fixed seed set S, temperature T, identical prompt.
  Step 2 — The SAME candidate pool is passed to both selection arms (shared-pool control; no resampling between arms, so differences reflect the criterion, not sampling variance).
  Step 3 — Arm EM: select ŷ_EM(q) = the candidate matching the largest number of co-sampled candidates under exact string match (mode). Ties broken deterministically (Section 5).
  Step 4 — Arm MinED: select ŷ_MinED(q) = argmin_i Σ_j d(y_i, y_j), d = normalized Levenshtein on lightly normalized outputs (lowercase, strip whitespace/punctuation, extract final answer line). 
  Step 5 — Score both selections with the same EM-to-gold metric: correct(ŷ, gold) via standard BBH scoring (exact letter match for MC; exact/regex match with the official BBH answer extraction for free-form).
Reference lines: pass@N(q) — the pool contains at least one gold-matching candidate — computed on the same pools as a ceiling reference; single-sample greedy baseline (N=1) as a floor reference.

3.2 Sample-size configuration:
- Primary configuration: N = 8 candidates per question, one seed set.
- N ablation: N ∈ {4, 8, 16} on a fixed subsample (or full set if compute allows) to test robustness of the MinED−EM delta to pool size.
- Repeated seeds: 3 independent seed sets at N = 8 to estimate sampling variance and support seed-level inference.
- Expected scale: BBH has 6,511 questions (4,723 MC + 1,788 free-form). Total generations ≈ 6,511 × 8 × 3 seeds ≈ 156k samples — feasible for one model family; the design does not require execution here.

3.3 Arms and conditions summary:
  • E1 (primary): EM selection, N = 8, all 27 tasks.
  • E2 (primary): MinED selection, N = 8, all 27 tasks (same pools as E1).
  • E3 (sensitivity): MinED variants (Section 6), same pools.
  • E4 (ablation): N ∈ {4, 16}, both arms, same pools per N.
  • References: pass@N, greedy N=1 baseline.
  • Determinism check: greedy single-sample vs. N=1 sampling sanity check.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. CONTROLS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- Shared candidate pool (identical samples fed to both arms) — the core control isolating the criterion effect.
- Identical prompts, decoding parameters, model checkpoint, and scoring pipeline across arms.
- Fixed, pre-registered tie-breaking (Section 5) applied identically in both arms.
- Deterministic scoring: single scoring script with a fixed answer-extraction/normalization function, applied post-selection; extraction errors are logged, not hand-corrected post hoc.
- Scoring pipeline validated on a small held-out hand-labeled subset (e.g., 50 questions/task) before full scoring — a calibration control, run only if the design were executed.
- Blinding: the analysis script computes both arms' scores without the analyst inspecting intermediate per-task results before freezing the analysis code.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. TIE-BREAKING AND DETERMINISM RULES (pre-registered)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- EM arm ties among tied-frequency candidates: (i) earliest occurrence index in the pool; if still tied, (ii) lexicographically smallest string.
- MinED arm ties among tied total distance: same two-stage rule (earliest index, then lexicographic).
- Duplicate clusters: collapsed before distance computation (duplicates contribute identical distance values; selection over distinct strings, index of first occurrence kept).
- MC tasks: edit distance computed on the extracted answer letter/token, not the full CoT trace; EM/mode likewise on the extracted token.
- All random seeds, tie-break rules, and normalization functions fixed in the pre-registration before any (hypothetical) run.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6. SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS OVER MinED VARIANTS (per researcher refinement)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Because the precise MinED formulation is unstated in the available context, the design does not hinge on one variant. Four pre-registered variants, all on the same pools:
  V1: summed pairwise distance — argmin_i Σ_j d(y_i, y_j).
  V2: medoid (equivalent to V1 by symmetry of Levenshtein — reported to confirm equivalence rather than assumed).
  V3: summed distance with normalization disabled (raw character edit distance on the final answer string).
  V4: summed distance with stronger normalization (case-fold, strip punctuation/whitespace, canonical answer extraction).
Interpretation rule: the conclusion "MinED outperforms EM" is reported as robust if ALL variants agree in direction; if variants disagree, the result is reported as formulation-sensitive with per-variant deltas shown. This converts U1/U2-style ambiguity into an explicit analysis output instead of a blocker.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7. METRICS AND ANALYSIS PLAN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Primary endpoint (pre-registered): overall BBH exact-match accuracy (micro over all 6,511 questions, all 27 tasks), MinED arm vs. EM arm, N = 8.
Secondary endpoints (pre-registered): (a) free-form subset (4 tasks) accuracy — the expected locus of any effect per A3; (b) MC subset (23 tasks) accuracy — expected ≈ 0 delta, serving as a built-in negative control; (c) per-task accuracies (27 values) for heterogeneity analysis.
Supporting metrics: arm agreement rate (fraction of questions where arms pick the same candidate); pass@N ceiling; greedy baseline; per-task selection-margin distributions (e.g., MinED winner's distance gap).

Statistical tests:
  1. Paired per-question test on the full benchmark: McNemar's test on the discordant-pair counts (MinED-only correct vs. EM-only correct), aggregated across all questions.
  2. Cluster-aware inference: questions are nested in tasks, so also run a cluster bootstrap (resample tasks with replacement, B = 10,000) on the accuracy delta; report bootstrap 95% CI for Δ = acc(MinED) − acc(EM). A seed-level check (3 seeds) supplements this: report per-seed deltas and their sign consistency.
  3. Stratified analyses: McNemar + cluster bootstrap separately on the free-form subset and the MC subset.
  4. Heterogeneity: per-task Δ with 95% CIs (bootstrap within task), displayed as a forest plot; task-level random-effects summary as a robustness check on the micro aggregate.
  5. Multiplicity: the two pre-registered endpoints are reported with no p-value correction (both are confirmatory); all other per-task/per-variant tests are labeled exploratory.
Decision rule (operationalizing "outperforms", per the approved sketch): MinED is declared to outperform EM if (i) Δ > 0 on the primary endpoint with McNemar p < 0.05 and a cluster-bootstrap CI excluding 0, AND (ii) direction is consistent across all MinED variants (Section 6) and across seeds. If (i) holds only on the free-form subset, report a qualified finding: "MinED outperforms EM on free-form BBH tasks, with ≈parity on MC tasks" — which is the mechanistically expected outcome under A3 and still answers the question truthfully.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FEASIBILITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- This environment is design-only by construction: /workspace contains only task.json; network is disabled; no GPU, datasets, or ML libraries are installed. No execution is required or attempted, consistent with the task contract.
- If executed elsewhere, the design is standard and feasible: BBH is public (~6.5k questions); the pipeline is (i) sampling, (ii) two pure-Python selection functions (Levenshtein via a standard DP implementation over ≤16 strings of short answer length; pairwise cost ≈ N²/2 distances per question — trivial CPU cost), (iii) one scoring script, (iv) McNemar + bootstrap analysis in scipy/numpy. The only substantial cost is candidate generation (~156k samples at N = 8 × 3 seeds), which is a single-model inference job and can be reduced by using the N = 4 primary configuration if compute-limited (the N ablation already covers this).
- Feasibility risks and mitigations: degenerate candidate pools (all candidates identical → arms identical by construction; these questions contribute zero discordant pairs and are counted in the denominator); free-form answer-extraction errors (mitigated by the calibration control in Section 4); MC-task degeneracy of MinED (handled by stratified endpoints rather than excluded, so the primary endpoint remains over the full benchmark as fixed by the task context).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. WHAT WOULD VALIDATE OR FALSIFY THE DESIGN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- Falsification of the hypothesis: Δ ≤ 0 or CI includes 0 on the primary endpoint → MinED does not outperform EM on BBH (report as negative/null).
- Design self-check: the MC subset should show near-zero Δ; a large positive/negative MC delta would indicate a scoring or tie-breaking artifact rather than a genuine criterion effect, triggering a pipeline audit before interpretation.
- The pass@N ceiling contextualizes the practical size of any win: Δ is more meaningful when pass@N − EM is large (headroom exists).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTIES (explicitly non-blocking; documented as assumptions)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- Exact EM-selection formulation in the source paper (mode selection assumed under A1; alternatives such as "select candidate matching the greedy output" would be a one-line change to the arm definition).
- MinED formulation (handled by Section 6 sensitivity analysis).
- Model identity, temperature, and prompt wording (within-model paired design makes conclusions conditional on these choices; a second model family is listed as an optional robustness extension, not a requirement).
- Free-form scoring variant (exact match vs. contains) — fixed to standard BBH scoring in the design; noted as assumption.
- Whether the paper's own numbers should be mirrored — the design specifies a de novo evaluation; if the researcher later wants replication, only Section 3.2 parameters change.

This is the complete deliverable: design, rationale, controls, analysis plan, and feasibility. Nothing has been run and no results are claimed.

disclosed_researcher_facts.text: Evaluate whether the proposed MinED (Minimum Edit Distance) method for alignment criteria outperforms the EM (Exact Matching) method on the BBH benchmark.
Compare the effectiveness of MinED and EM alignment criteria by measuring performance on BBH tasks.
- Big-Bench Hard (BBH) including 23 multiple-choice tasks and 4 free-form generation tasks.
- Covers algorithmic reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, natural language understanding, world knowledge, and multilingual tasks.
